title: Overview: the big ideas
summary: The chapter's key concepts and how its sections fit together.

blocks.md: Welcome to **Engineering Physical AI** (Vol IV). This overview gives you the chapter's big ideas before the section-by-section lessons. Read the claims once, flip the flashcards, then take the warm-up quiz: it is fine to miss questions here, the lessons that follow fill the gaps.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Engineering Physical AI, Purpose
blocks.md: The learned model is the part of a physical machine that is easiest to improve and easiest to score, so it attracts most of the effort. Useful service depends on everything around it as well. The body must sustain the task across loads, surfaces, and hours of duty. The learned behavior must hold in the states its own actions create. Each proposal must be admitted, corrected, or refused before the motion it asks for is already under way.

nodes.label: From a Better Prediction to Useful Servi

rows: The method transfers to an unfamiliar machine as four ordered questions (what the task cannot undo and which measured bound excludes it, whether closed-loop evidence covers the enforced envelope, which independent path admits each proposal, and what evidence bounds the authority granted), not as the warehouse machine's numbers.

A premise no onboard sensor reports is not the envelope's monitored unknown, so it is bound to a standing restriction, an accountable owner, and a predeclared closure test, chosen among responses (probe, restrict, add sensing, accept by judgment) by the claim each can support.

Open register entries fall into classes by the evidence they lack (an unmeasured observable, an evaluation deficit, a theoretical deficit) or by a scope mismatch that no evidence inside the present architecture repairs, and the class, not the urgency, selects the next experiment, with each restriction priced against the campaign that would retire it.

When two states that need different responses produce identical observations until the action deadline, no model on that channel can separate them, and the latest useful observation is set by braking distance over speed.

A shield's per-command guarantee becomes a hazard-rate claim only conditionally, lambda_sys <= lambda_h(1 - c) + lambda_cc, and observed fleet rates already include the shield, so multiplying them by an interception factor double-counts.
